neighbours.label: A single person as the subject of an embedded clause (' person' after 'when/after the', a first name such as Kate after 'whether/if'), or ' personal' before an abstract noun; context-dependent, not the bare tokens
fire: The sugar enters the blood a short while after the person eats the fruit.
Reporters kept asking whether Kate was going to attend.
Many believe this herb is a good remedy for personal strength.
The drug only works when the person takes it with food.
The guard would not tell us if Kate is still inside.
The alcohol affects judgment well before the person feels it.
Staff at the clinic refused to confirm whether Kate had arrived.
The vitamin is absorbed more slowly when the person sleeps badly.
quiet: The sugar enters the blood a short while after the horse eats the fruit.
Reporters kept asking whether the plane was going to land.
Many believe this herb is a good remedy for sore muscles.
The drug only works when the tablet dissolves in water.
The guard would not tell us if the gate is still open.
The alcohol evaporates well before the sauce thickens.
Staff at the clinic refused to confirm whether the shipment had arrived.
The vitamin is absorbed more slowly when the weather turns cold.

short: lone person subject in a sub-clause
notes: Card: ' person', ' personal', ' Kate' x3, ' Katie', ' self'; the + direction suppresses ' and' (the - pole is 'you and your family', 'X and colleagues'). Probes: 'after the person drinks' 0.90, 'for personal power' 0.82, 'whether Kate was' 0.88; 'Each person must' 0.02, 'Kate and William' 0.10, 'personal training' 0.16, 'personal belongings' 0.15, Linda 0.02, dog 0.01.
